authors: Nimick DA, Gammons CH, Cleasby TE, Madison JP, Skaar D, Brick CM
site: High Ore Creek (site 13), 2-4 Aug 1999
measure: dissolved, temperature held constant (pH coefficient from log10 C ~ pH + T)
location_in_paper: Fig. 4 (metal) paired by time with Fig. 9b (pH), 9e (T)
extraction_notes: Multiple OLS log10 C = a + b*pH + c*T: b=-0.3785+/-0.0946, c=-0.02690+/-0.00264 per C (p=5.1e-13), model R2=0.89; r(pH,T)=+0.70. Points extracted from the vector figure drawing (exact marker coordinates, not pixels); legend markers removed; extracted extremes match Table 1 diel ranges; r2 values recomputed here reproduce Table 3 (e.g. Prickly Pear Zn-pH 0.86 vs 0.80 reported, Zn-T 0.88 vs 0.83). SE from OLS ignores serial autocorrelation of a time series, so it is too small; treat as a lower bound. Authors: adsorption (pH- and temperature-dependent) is the only single mechanism explaining both As (anion, max late afternoon) and Cd/Mn/Zn (cations, max after sunrise); Mn redox and biological uptake also possible; Zn correlates more strongly with T (R2 0.83-0.91) than pH (0.62-0.80) but Fig. 10 amplitude analysis favours pH (p=0.003 vs 0.061). Cu inconsistent (colloidal). No cycle in acidic streams (pH<5.4).  High Ore Creek is a losing reach (no groundwater inflow); pH range only 0.26 units, pH maximum lasts 1-2 h while the nighttime minimum persists 6-10 h, so concentration tracks T more closely than pH.
